title: Theme Gallery
description: Fifteen chapters, one per theme this mod ships apart from the default. Click them in the
sidebar and the canvas changes colour -- no command, no setting to find first.
Every chapter below names a theme of its own in the 'theme' field beside its title, and every
chapter has the same six quests in the same six positions. That is the whole design and it is
deliberate rather than lazy: if the chapters differed in layout as well as in colour, a
difference you saw while clicking between them could be either, and an exhibit that varies two
things shows nothing.
What a chapter's theme covers is the canvas and the quest overlay -- the graph, its nodes,
their rings and connectors, the backdrop, and the panel you get when you open a quest. What it
does NOT cover is the frame around them: the sidebar, the header, the title, the buttons and
the tooltips are drawn in YOUR theme, whatever chapter you are standing in. So opening a
violet chapter shows a violet canvas inside an otherwise unchanged book, and both are visible
at once.
That split is why a chapter's theme never fights with yours. Yours is the book; the
chapter's is its own picture, and neither can be overruled by the other because they never
describe the same pixels.
The theme the book itself is drawn in is a setting rather than a button, and it is not one of
these chapters. Out of the box it is called 'default': Modern's colours with square corners,
which is what you are reading this in unless you have changed it. It lives in
config/armature/appearance.json, and a modpack can ask for a different one for players who
have never chosen -- your own choice always wins over a pack's.
So the sidebar, the header, the buttons and the tooltips are 'default' while you stand in a
violet chapter, and they keep their own square corners. The chapters below are the OTHER
fifteen themes: every one this build ships apart from the default, which is the frame itself.
Corners are the most visible thing a theme decides after its colours, and they are worth
looking at because they show up in two places at once. The book's own panel is drawn in your
theme -- square, by default -- while the quest overlay is inside the chapter's scope, so open
a quest here and its panel is rounded to whatever this chapter asks for. Tome and End round at
8, Modern at 4, Obsidian and Monochrome at 2, and Vanilla Plus, High Contrast and Terminal at
0. Tome against Vanilla Plus is the pair to flip between: the same panel, drawn by the same
code, and the corners are the whole difference.
Animations come from a theme as well -- how long a transition lasts and what curve it uses --
so Vanilla Plus, High Contrast and Terminal have a motion of zero and snap, where Modern eases
over 140ms. There is a switch that turns motion off altogether and overrides every theme, but
it is not on this screen any more; it belongs with the other accessibility settings. What is
worth knowing here is that the precedence is deliberate: a reskin must not be able to
re-enable animation for somebody who cannot comfortably use it.
The fifteen themes these chapters cover, in the order the catalogue lists them: Modern, Tome,
Vanilla Plus, High Contrast, Monochrome, Paper, Obsidian, Amethyst, Copper, Redstone, Nether,
End, Deep Dark, Terminal, Neon.
